subject: Clarify surcharge rounding and long-history context slices
messages:

Subject: Question on surcharge rounding with long-history contexts

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. One procurement follow-up: our billing team is trying to reconcile usage on the pilot and they see a small recurring surcharge line when we hit long-history retrievals (10k+ tokens). It looks like two things are interacting: (1) your per-call minimum/rounding behavior and (2) an applied "surcharge" for long-context compute in the pricing sheet.

Specifically: when a single end-user session spans many short calls that collectively exceed the 10k context threshold, the invoice shows per-call rounding up to the quantum and then an additional long-context surcharge on top of the aggregated tokens. That double-counting is leading to a ~7% delta vs our expected model.

Can you confirm how Redwood handles:
- token accounting across interleaved short calls that share the same conversation history (do you coalesce these for the long-context surcharge?)
- the order of operations for rounding/minimums vs surcharge application (is the surcharge calculated before or after rounding?)

If useful, I can share a sample extract from our logs. Procurement wants clarity before we sign off.

Best,
Olivia
BrightCart — Head of Integrations

Subject: Re: Question on surcharge rounding with long-history contexts

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachment, that helps. Short answer up front: we do not intentionally double-charge tokens, but the interaction you describe can appear that way depending on how sessions are surfaced in invoicing. Below is a concise explanation plus two concrete options we can apply for your invoice reconciliation.

How it currently works (high level):
- Metering: each API call is tokenized and charged to the nearest billing quantum per the contract (example: 50-token quantum).
- Long-context surcharge: applied when the active context window for a logical conversation exceeds the configured threshold (10k). The surcharge is a multiplier applied to the aggregate compute for that logical conversation.
- Coalescing: coalescing of short calls into a single logical conversation happens in our billing pipeline only when we can deterministically map calls to the same conversation id and the calls arrive within the billing window. If your client sessions are fragmented across multiple connection ids (e.g., different frontend shards), calls may not be coalesced and rounding can inflate totals before the surcharge is evaluated.

Order of operations (current system):
1) Raw tokens per call are measured and rounded up to the quantum.
2) We sum rounded tokens for calls attributed to the same conversation within the billing window.
3) If the summed context exceeds the long-context threshold, the surcharge multiplier is applied to that summed amount.

So the surcharge is applied after per-call rounding and aggregation — which is why a fragmentation pattern can create the apparent double effect you saw.

Options to resolve for BrightCart:
A) "Conversation coalescing" override: we can enable an attribution rule for your account (use your session id header) so calls get coalesced server-side before rounding. This typically reduces the rounding noise.
B) Invoice post-process: apply a reconciliation credit that reverse-engineers the effective quantization if you provide the session-level logs (we can run the same aggregation but with rounding deferred to after coalescing).

Next steps: 1) if you can share a small sample extract (CSV) showing session ids and timestamps, we can run an internal reconciliation and produce a sample corrected invoice. 2) If procurement prefers, we can add a short-term credit while we instrument the coalescing override.

Cc'ing Ben (billing lead) and Aditya (pricing) to propose the exact language/credit.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

On Fri, May 27, 2026 at 6:03 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> So the surcharge is applied after per-call rounding and aggregation — which is why a fragmentation pattern can create the apparent double effect you saw.

Adding a few concrete bullets on the reconciliation side and suggested wording for a credit:
- If we enable "session-id coalescing" at the billing layer, tokens are aggregated first, then rounded once — this eliminates the per-call rounding blow-up for fragmented clients. Implementation is configuration-only and can be retroactive for invoice runs if we have the session-level mapping.
- If BrightCart needs an immediate fix for the outstanding pilot invoice, propose: a one-time reconciliation credit equal to (sum_{sessions} (rounded_sum_per_call - rounded_after_coalesce)). For an estimate, we typically see 3–9% uplift on noisy frontends; your sample shows ~7% as Olivia noted.
- For contract language going forward, recommend: "Long-context surcharge applies to aggregated conversation tokens after platform-side coalescing; vendor reserves the right to exclude clear multi-shard fragmentation cases from surcharge assessment upon customer-provided session traces."

I'll draft the credit appendix if you want to offer it. Aditya, please confirm pricing impact and whether we should cap the credit amount (we usually cap at one invoice month or $X for pilots).

Ben
VP, Revenue Operations
